screening_decisions.reason: This is a global burden estimation study using published data, not a randomized controlled trial comparing early vs delayed ART initiation.
This is a case series of 5 children with cryptococcal meningitis, not a randomized controlled trial.
This study examines toxicity of amphotericin B-based induction therapy, not comparing early vs delayed ART initiation.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of IRIS incidence, not a primary RCT comparing ART timing.
This is a letter to the editor commenting on methodological issues, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a methodological paper about GRADE system, not a clinical trial.
This is a prospective observational study of CM-IRIS incidence, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing.
This is a cohort study from Latin America examining outcomes, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a methodological guideline paper about GRADE system, not a clinical trial.
This appears to be a letter or commentary citing other studies, not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a consensus paper proposing case definitions for cryptococcal IRIS, not a randomized controlled trial.
This describes an operational program offering early ART to in-patients with various OIs, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a randomized controlled trial that compared earlier ART initiation (1-2 weeks after diagnosis) vs deferred ART initiation (5 weeks after diagnosis) in HIV-infected adults with cryptococcal meningitis. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a global burden estimation study using modeling approaches, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a review paper about antifungal drug access issues, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a letter expressing concerns about another randomized study, not a primary randomized controlled trial itself.
This is an observational study examining amphotericin B-related toxicities, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing.
This is a descriptive longitudinal observational study of natural history, not a randomized controlled trial.

While this is an RCT comparing early vs deferred ART, it included multiple opportunistic infections (PJP 63%, CM only 12%, bacterial 12%). The population is not specifically HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis as required by selection criteria.
This appears to be a commentary or review article describing another RCT (Bouleware et al.), not a primary randomized controlled trial itself.

The abstract does not clearly describe a randomized controlled trial design. It appears to be an observational analysis of mortality rates between early and deferred ART groups without clear randomization.
This is a letter or editorial discussing treatment strategies, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a randomized treatment-strategy trial conducted in Botswana that compared ART initiation within 7 days vs after 28 days in HIV-infected adults with cryptococcal meningitis. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing immediate vs deferred ART, but the population was asymptomatic HIV patients with CD4 >500 cells/mm3, not HIV-positive people with cryptococcal meningitis.
This is a prospective observational study of symptomatic relapse after fluconazole monotherapy, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing.
This is an observational study examining IRIS in HIV-Cryptococcus coinfection, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing.
This is a review article about cryptococcal meningitis epidemiology and treatment, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a prospective multicenter observational study of cryptococcal IRIS, not a randomized controlled trial comparing ART timing.

This is a prospective open-label randomized clinical trial conducted in Zimbabwe that compared early ART (within 72 hours after CM diagnosis) vs delayed ART (after 10 weeks) in HIV-positive individuals with cryptococcal meningitis. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a comprehensive review article about cryptococcal meningitis epidemiology, immunology, diagnosis and therapy, not a randomized controlled trial.
